q-28653.name: Question 1
q-28653.worked_solution:
The angle ${45}^{∘}$ is special, and its trigonometric ratios have the values

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\,\operatorname{tan}⁡{45}^{∘}=1,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

Also, note that ${sin}^{2}⁡{45}^{∘}$ means $(\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘})^{2},$ ${cos}^{2}⁡{45}^{∘}$ means $(\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘})^{2}$ and  ${tan}^{2}⁡{45}^{∘}$ means $(\operatorname{tan}⁡{45}^{∘})^{2}.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}5{cos}^{2}⁡{45}^{∘}+3{sin}^{2}⁡{45}^{∘}-7{tan}^{2}⁡{45}^{∘} & = \\ 5(\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘})^{2}+3(\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘})^{2}-7(\operatorname{tan}⁡{45}^{∘})^{2} & = \\ 5{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}+3{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}-7(1)^{2} & = \\ 8{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}-7 & = \\ 8(\frac{2}{4})-7 & = \\ 4-7 & = \\ -3. & \end{aligned}
$$

q-244566.name: Question 4
q-244566.worked_solution:
Remember that $csc$ is the reciprocal of $sin.$ So

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡C=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡C}.
$$

We have that $m∠C={45}^{∘},$ which is a special angle, and its sine has the value

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡C=\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{csc}⁡C & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡C} \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-266630.name: Question 6
q-266630.worked_solution:
Remember that $sec$  is the reciprocal of $cos,$  $csc$ is the reciprocal of $sin$  and $cot$  is the reciprocal of $tan.$
So, we have

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡{60}^{∘}=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{60}^{∘}},\,\operatorname{csc}⁡{30}^{∘}=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}},\,\operatorname{cot}⁡{30}^{∘}=\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡{30}^{∘}}.
$$

The angle ${60}^{∘}$ and ${30}^{∘}$ are special, and its trigonometric ratios have the values

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡{60}^{∘}=\frac{1}{2},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}=\frac{1}{2},\,\operatorname{tan}⁡{30}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}6\operatorname{sec}⁡{60}^{∘}+3\operatorname{csc}⁡{30}^{∘}+\operatorname{cot}⁡{30}^{∘} & = \\ 6(\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{60}^{∘}})+3(\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}})+\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡{30}^{∘}} & = \\ \frac{6}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{60}^{∘}}+\frac{3}{\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}}+\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡{30}^{∘}} & = \\ \frac{6}{(\frac{1}{2})}+\frac{3}{(\frac{1}{2})}+\frac{1}{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})} & = \\ 12+6+\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}} & = \\ 18+\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}} & = \\ 18+\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} & = \\ 18+\sqrt{3}. & \end{aligned}
$$

The angles 45∘, 90∘ and 30∘ are special angles, and their trigonometric ratios have the values sin⁡45∘=22,sin⁡90∘=1,sin⁡30∘=12.

The angles ${45}^{∘},$ ${90}^{∘}$ and ${0}^{∘}$ are special angles, and their trigonometric ratios have the values

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡{90}^{∘}=0,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡{0}^{∘}=1.
$$

Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘}+\operatorname{cos}⁡{90}^{∘}+\operatorname{cos}⁡{0}^{∘} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+0+1 & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}+2}{2}. & \end{aligned}
$$
